redaction.segregability.summary: If a record contains both disclosable and non-disclosable information, the authority shall provide the disclosable information and delete the non-disclosable information from the record before release.

Redaction.r1.city_config: The exemption library content (shared with Denial.nreason); segregability default applies in 25 states.

redaction.mandatory_pii.summary: An authority shall not provide access to personally identifiable information containing an individual's account/customer number with a financial institution (including credit card, debit card, checking, or draft account numbers) unless specifically required by law.

redaction.protected_person.summary: A law enforcement authority receiving a request for a record containing information (name, address, phone, voice recording, handwriting sample) that would identify an informant shall delete that portion, or withhold the record if it cannot be segregated, unless the legal custodian determines at t…

production.format_and_medium.summary: If a requester appears personally to request a copy of a copyable record, the authority may, at its option, permit the requester to copy the record or provide the requester with a copy substantially as readable as the original.

production.av_media_specific.summary: If a handwritten record or voice recording must be withheld/redacted under s. 19.36(8)(b) because the handwriting or voice would identify an informant, the authority shall provide the requester, upon request, a transcript of the record or information, if otherwise subject to disclosure.

For a record that is a comprehensible audio recording, the requester has a right to a copy substantially as audible as the original; the authority may instead provide a transcript if the requester so requests.
For a record that is a video recording, the requester has a right to a copy substantially as good as the original.

production.inspection_access.summary: An authority that maintains regular office hours at the location where records are kept shall permit access to those records at all times during those office hours, unless otherwise specifically authorized by law.
An authority without regular office hours at the records location may require at least 48 hours' written or oral notice of intent to inspect or copy before permitting access.
production.inspection_access.clock_spec: floor: 48 hours advance written or oral notice of intent to inspect/copy

production.inspection_access.summary: As an alternative, such an authority may establish a period of at least 2 consecutive hours per week during which access is permitted, and may then require 24 hours' advance written or oral notice of intent to inspect or copy.
production.inspection_access.clock_spec: floor: 2 consecutive hours per week access window; may require 24 hours advance notice

production.inspection_access.summary: The authority shall provide facilities comparable to those used by its employees to inspect, copy, and abstract the record during established office hours, but is not required to purchase/lease equipment or provide a separate room.

production.no_duty_to_create_or_convert.summary: For a record not in a readily comprehensible form, the requester has a right to a copy of the information assembled and reduced to written form on paper.

Except as necessary to comply with pars. (c)-(e) or s. 19.36(6), the law does not require an authority to create a new record by extracting information from existing records and compiling it in a new format.

eligibility.incarcerated_requester_exclu.summary: A committed or incarcerated person is not a 'requester' with general access rights unless the requested record contains specific references to that person or his or her minor children (for whom physical placement has not been denied) and the record is otherwise accessible to the person by law.

eligibility.record_subject_self_access.summary: A requester who is the individual (or person authorized by the individual) has an additional right to inspect and copy personally identifiable information pertaining to that individual, subject to the enumerated exceptions (enforcement/investigation records, life/safety, informant, security, etc.).

intake.identity_requirement.summary: A requester may be required to show acceptable identification whenever the requested record is kept at a private residence, or whenever security reasons or federal law/regulations so require.

eligibility.any_person.summary: Any requester (any person requesting inspection or copies of a record) has a right to inspect any record, except as otherwise provided by law.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: A request may not be refused because the requester is unwilling to state the purpose of the request.

eligibility.no_residency_requirement.summary: No residency or citizenship qualification is imposed on a requester; any requester has the right to inspect any record.

eligibility.no_identity_requirement.summary: A request may not be refused because the requester is unwilling to be identified, except where acceptable identification may be required for records kept at a private residence or where security/federal law requires.

fee.waiver.summary: An authority may provide copies without charge or at a reduced charge where it determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest.

custody.contractor_and_thirdparty_custod.summary: A local information technology authority holding a law enforcement record only for storage/processing is not the legal custodian; the custodian is the authority for which the record is stored, and the IT authority shall deny any portion of a request relating to a local law enforcement record.

Clarification.deny.note: Deny-as-vague is narrower than reasonably-describes membership: TN·NJ·OH, OK only after SB 535 engagement (diagram legend, v2.2).

Records-Search.prog.label: BUT extraction/programming of EXISTING

production.no_duty_to_create_or_convert.summary: For a record not in a readily comprehensible form, the requester has a right to a copy of the information assembled and reduced to written form on paper.

Except as necessary to comply with pars. (c)-(e) or s. 19.36(6), the law does not require an authority to create a new record by extracting information from existing records and compiling it in a new format.

Records-Search.prog.note: Programming-≠-creation loop is TX 552.231 only; the broader no-duty-to-create concept (16 states) is context, not an activator.

special_records.special_production_const.summary: For a record whose form does not permit copying, the requester has a right to inspect it; the authority may permit the requester to photograph it, and if the requester requests a photograph be provided, the authority shall provide a good quality photograph.
The inspection/copy rights in pars. (a)-(c), (e) and (f) do not apply to a record that has been or will be promptly published with copies offered for sale or distribution.
A legal custodian may impose reasonable restrictions on the manner of access to an original record if the record is irreplaceable or easily damaged.
A requester shall comply with any regulations or restrictions upon access to or use of information that are specifically prescribed by law.

redaction.personnel_privacy_process.summary: If an authority decides to permit access to a specified record (employee disciplinary-investigation records, records obtained by subpoena/search warrant, or private-employer records about an employee), it shall, before permitting access and within 3 days after deciding to permit access, serve wri…
redaction.personnel_privacy_process.clock_spec: sets-deadline: within 3 days after the decision to permit access

redaction.personnel_privacy_process.summary: An authority shall not provide access to a requested record within 12 days of sending a record-subject notice under s. 19.356(2)(a); if the record subject commences an action, the authority shall not release during the pendency of the action (and through any appeal/review period).
redaction.personnel_privacy_process.clock_spec: sets-deadline: no release within 12 days of sending the 19.356(2)(a) notice; further hold during pendency of any action/appeal

redaction.personnel_privacy_process.summary: If an authority decides to permit access to a record relating to a record subject who is an officer/employee holding a local or state public office, it shall within 3 days serve written notice on the subject; the subject may within 5 days augment the record with written comments/documentation, an…
redaction.personnel_privacy_process.clock_spec: sets-deadline: notice within 3 days of decision to permit access; record subject may augment within 5 days after receipt of notice

II or its annotations; color copies fall under the same actual/necessary/direct reproduction-cost ceiling of § 19.35(3)(a). A city's color rate may reflect the higher actual cost of color reproduction but nothing more.

dup.oversized.rate.notes: No distinct oversized/nonstandard-page provision; oversized reproduction is governed by the § 19.35(3)(a) actual-cost standard (or (3)(b) photographing standard where the form does not permit copying). City sets any oversized rate under actual, necessary and direct cost.

dup.specialty.rate.notes: Photographs of non-copyable records: actual/necessary/direct cost of photographing and photographic processing (§ 19.35(3)(b)). dup.tiers.notes: Structured negative. Wisconsin has a pure actual-cost regime with no volume bands. A city may design tiers only insofar as each tier stays within the actual, necessary and direct cost ceiling of § 19.35(3)(a).

Note also § 19.35(1)(L): no duty to create a new record by extracting an…

labor.billableWhen.unit: USD (location-cost chargeability threshold: location/search labor chargeable only if its actual cost is $50 or more)
labor.billableWhen.authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(c); Milwaukee Journal Sentinel v. City of Milwaukee, 2012 WI 65; Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(h)
labor.billableWhen.notes: Engine shape: (1) location/search labor: chargeable only when the location cost reaches $50 (below $50 it is free, and per WI-0037 notes sub-$50 location costs may not be folded into reproduction charges); (2) review/redaction labor: never chargeable for general records (Milwaukee Journal Sentine…

labor.overheadPct.notes: Structured negative. No overhead multiplier is authorized. The statutory standard is 'actual, necessary and DIRECT cost' — the word 'direct' cuts against loading indirect/overhead costs onto any fee, though the statute does not expressly address a percentage. A city should not configure an overhe…

labor.increment.label: Labor time increment + rounding
labor.increment.notes: Structured negative. Any billing increment a city adopts must still keep the resulting charge within actual, necessary and direct cost (§ 19.35(3)(a)-(c)); an increment that systematically overshoots actual cost would exceed the ceiling.

rules.freeLaborHours.label: Free labor hours per request
rules.freeLaborHours.notes: Structured negative. Wisconsin's functional analogue is a COST threshold, not an hours threshold: location labor is free until its cost reaches $50 (§ 19.35(3)(c), resolved at labor.billableWhen). Do not convert $50 into an hours figure.

One narrow statutory estimate gate exists: § 19.35(3)(h)7 makes a prior WRITTEN estimate a precondition of charging the LE A/V redaction fee (any amount — no threshold; captured in WI-9001). DOJ guidance encourage…

estimate.requesterResponseDays.label: Requester must respond to an estimate within N days (else withdrawn)
estimate.requesterResponseDays.notes: Structured negative. Defers in practice to city policy; state law is silent.

estimate.revisionNotifyPercent.label: Revised estimate required when actual exceeds estimate by N%
estimate.revisionNotifyPercent.notes: Structured negative. The final charge is independently capped at actual, necessary and direct cost regardless of any estimate.

estimate.validityDays.label: Estimate validity period (days)
estimate.validityDays.notes: Structured negative. Defers in practice to city policy.

rules.deposit.percent.notes: Structured negative. § 19.35(3)(f) permits prepayment of 'any fee or fees' — i.e., up to 100% of the (reasonably estimated) total; no statutory percentage ceiling below that.

rules.minFee.notes: Structured negative. A flat minimum fee that exceeds actual, necessary and direct cost on a small request would violate the § 19.35(3)(a) ceiling — do not configure one for Wisconsin.

media.label: Electronic media (CD/DVD/USB) charge

certification.label: Certification / certified-copy charge
certification.notes: The records law sets NO certification rate. Operative rule is a gate: an UNREQUESTED certification may not be charged to the requester (WI-9003). A requested certification's charge, if any, comes from a record-specific fee statute (via the § 19.35(3)(a) 'otherwise established by law' clause) or s…

av.label: Audio/video: per recording, per minute, free minutes
av.notes: No per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes values anywhere. Copies of audio ((1)(c)) and video ((1)(d)) records are charged as reproduction at actual, necessary and direct cost ((3)(a)). Law enforcement agencies (including municipal police) may additionally charge actual A/V REDACTION cost und…

commercial.label: Commercial-purpose schedule (surcharge %, labor becomes chargeable)
commercial.authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35 (searched; no general commercial schedule); cf. § 19.35(3)(h)3.a
commercial.notes: Structured negative for a commercial schedule; § 19.35(1)(i) generally bars conditioning access on stated purpose (and examination of records cannot be denied for commercial purpose, 58 Atty. waiver.label: Fee waiver: grounds, mandatory vs discretionary, purpose statement, written denial, appeal
waiver.authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(e); George v. Record Custodian, 169 Wis. 2d 573, 485 N.W.2d 460 (Ct. App. 1992)
waiver.notes: Shape: single DISCRETIONARY waiver/reduction branch, sole statutory ground = authority's own public-interest determination. No mandatory waiver categories; no indigency waiver as of right (George v. Record Custodian, verbatim in WI-9004); no purpose-statement requirement (indeed § 19.35(1)(i) gen…

waiver.forfeiture.label: Late response forfeits the fee
waiver.forfeiture.notes: Structured negative. Do not confuse with § 19.37(4): the up-to-$1,000 forfeiture for arbitrary/capricious delay or excessive fees is a penalty paid to the state/county via AG/DA enforcement, not a waiver of the requester's fee. Wisconsin also has no fixed response deadline ('as soon as practicabl…

repeat.label: Repeat / aggregated requests (carry-forward, aggregation threshold)
repeat.notes: General repeat/aggregation regime: silent — no fee carry-forward and no request-aggregation threshold for ordinary records. The one statutory per-requestor counter is § 19.35(3)(h)3.b: a requester-ledger of audio/video requests per authority per calendar year; at more than 10 such requests, the n…

fee.copy_rate_per_page.summary: An authority may impose a fee for a copy of a record not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription, unless a fee is otherwise specifically established or authorized by law.
fee.copy_rate_per_page.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction and transcription

fee.labor_charge.authority: Wis. Stat. § 19.35(3)(am), created by 2023 Wis. Act 253
fee.labor_charge.summary: A law enforcement agency may impose a fee for the actual, necessary and direct cost of redacting recorded audio or video content to the extent redaction is required by law, but may not charge if: the requester (an individual) certifies non-commercial use; the event is an officer-involved shooting…
fee.labor_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of redacting recorded audio/video content

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: An authority may impose a fee for locating a record, not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of location, but only if that cost is $50 or more.
fee.actual_cost_basis.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of location; chargeable only if cost is $50 or more

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: If a record is produced or collected by a non-authority under contract with an authority, the authorized fee for a copy may not exceed the actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction or transcription incurred by that person, unless a fee is otherwise established by law.
fee.actual_cost_basis.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of reproduction/transcription incurred by the contractor

fee.delivery_charge.summary: An authority may impose a fee for the actual, necessary and direct cost of mailing or shipping any copy or photograph of a record that is mailed or shipped to the requester.
fee.delivery_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of mailing or shipping

fee.nonstandard_rate.summary: Where an authority provides a photograph of a record whose form does not permit copying, it may impose a fee not exceeding the actual, necessary and direct cost of photographing and photographic processing.
fee.nonstandard_rate.clock_spec: ceiling: actual, necessary and direct cost of photographing and photographic processing

fee.no_charge_categories.authority: Milwaukee Journal Sentinel v. City of Milwaukee, 2012 WI 65, 341 Wis. 2d 607
fee.no_charge_categories.summary: Redaction is not one of the four statutory fee tasks (reproduction/transcription, photographing/processing, locating, mailing/shipping); an authority generally may not impose a fee for the process of redacting information from a record.
fee.no_charge_categories.clock_spec: fixed: $0 for redaction/separation of information (general records)

custody.custodian_definition_and_role.summary: In the absence of a designation, the authority's highest ranking officer and the chief administrative officer (if any) are the legal custodians.

The legal custodian (or appointing authority) of records in a publicly owned/leased building shall designate one or more deputies to act as legal custodian in his or her absence or as otherwise required to respond to requests under s. 19.35(4).

custody.records_officer_designation.summary: Every authority not otherwise specified shall designate in writing one or more positions as legal custodian to fulfill the authority's duties under the subchapter, vested with full legal power to render decisions and carry out those duties.

intake.procedures_publication.summary: Each authority shall adopt, prominently display, and make available a notice describing its organization, the times/places and legal custodian from whom, and methods whereby, the public may obtain access to and copies of records, and the costs thereof; the notice shall separately identify each lo…

payment.advance_payment.summary: An authority may require prepayment of any fee(s) imposed under sub. (3) if the total amount exceeds $5.
payment.advance_payment.clock_spec: fixed: prepayment may be required when total fees exceed $5

payment.advance_payment.summary: If the requester is a prisoner (or person confined in a federal institution in this state) who failed to pay a fee for a previous request, the authority may require prepayment of both the previously owed amount and the current amount.

payment.advance_payment.authority: State ex rel. Hill v. Zimmerman, 196 Wis. 2d 419, 538 N.W.2d 608 (Ct. App. 1995)
payment.advance_payment.summary: The amount of prepayment required for copies may be based on a reasonable estimate.
